Thanks Priyom — appreciate the draft. Quick notes after an internal pass: 

1) The timeline in the second paragraph says "2 months to production"; for Greenstone it was closer to 10 weeks — can we change to "~10 weeks"?
2) The cost reduction number looks correct for our average workload but please change the sentence to note "average inference cost per 1M tokens" so it's clear what the metric refers to.
3) The quote attributed to our CTO (Aisha Patel) is fine but she prefers the phrase "reduced our inference spend" instead of "cut our inference cost".

I attached a short redline doc with a few inline edits and a suggested alternative quote. Legal is copied because they want to confirm the final quote language before we publish.

Attachments: greenstone-case-draft-v2-redlines.docx (docx)

Happy to do a quick review call Thursday if that helps — otherwise we'll aim to turn around formal sign-off once Legal confirms the final quote.

On Wed, Aug 5, 2026 at 08:03 Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood-inference.com> wrote:
> Marissa / Rachel — looping you in to pick up the quote approval and the small copy/metric tweaks Claire flagged.

All good from CS on the metrics. The 48% figure is the blended reduction across our production inference mix (batched and streaming), based on comparing their Jan-Feb baseline to the April steady state after we enabled prefix caching and quantized weights. "Average inference cost per 1M tokens" is an accurate description.

95th latency for their primary model (seq len 1024) sits at ~230ms post-optimization, p99 is ~420ms. If marketing wants to simplify, we can call out "median latency improved to ~130ms; p99 is ~420ms."

I can confirm numbers to Legal on a quick thread if they need the underlying spreadsheet. For the quote: Aisha's preferred wording in Claire's alternative is fine — minor tweak below to keep tone concise: 
"Redwood reduced our inference spend by 48% while improving latency across peak workloads."

Attaching the internal cost worksheet we used to calculate the 48% (internal_spreadsheet.csv).

Attachments: internal_spreadsheet.csv

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
